title: Synthetic eval capture for quantization-induced quality drift
creator: Amelia Chen
description: Summary: After the 1.21 quantization patch rolled to canary, we observed a reproducible quality drop for a cluster of domain prompts (finance + legal templates). Initial triage flagged higher token split variance and token ID reassignments when using the new quantized kernels, which in turn shifted embeddings and downstream completions. This ticket captures the work to (1) build targeted synthetic evals that reproduce the tokenizer+quantization interaction, (2) wire them into CI and canary gates, and (3) add durable regression tests so the same drift cannot silently ship in future config/model sweeps.
acceptance_criteria:
- Synthetic generator reproduces observed failure cases with >90% recall on historical incident traces.
- New evals run in CI for PRs touching quantization or tokenizer paths.
- Canary rollout pipeline includes the eval and will block or auto-revert if quality delta > 3% on defined metrics.
- Dashboard tile shows pre/post metrics for any candidate rollout using quantized kernels.

Also propose a fallback policy for canary rollouts: if eval fails, route 100% of traffic to previous non-quantized variant and notify SRE channel.

decision_log: 2025-02-16 Decision: Build targeted synthetic evals rather than expanding existing universal evals. Rationale: faster iteration and lower CI cost, able to capture tokenizer-quantization interaction specifically.
2025-02-18 Decision: Two-tier gating (fast CI smoke + nightly statistical canary). Rationale: balance developer velocity with safety of releases. Approved by Eng Leads.
2025-02-19 Decision: Use 'token split variance' and 'top-10 token probability shift' as primary signal; set initial block threshold at 3% weighted delta. Will iterate after 2 weeks of telemetry.
